agent_notes: This diff is not a security change but is worth flagging: it is the exact inverse of the just-made fix in commit 542d5dd ('General settings fields lived in a separate form from the Save button, so saving never submitted them'). The diff reverts triggarr/templates/settings.html from the fixed state (General inputs associated via form="settings-form" with the single instances form, id="settings-form") back to two independent <form method=post action=save_settings> elements: the General form (lines 18-90 in the new state) has no submit button of its own, and the per-app instances form (line 134) retains the only 'Save Settings' button but no longer carries the General fields. Per triggarr/web/routes.py save_settings() (lines 529-541), the 'general' config block is rebuilt unconditionally from form.get(...) with hardcoded fallback defaults (0, 1000, 30, 50, 60, 5, False) with no fallback to current_settings.general.* the way the per-app instance branch explicitly preserves existing instances when absent (lines 581-594). So clicking the only working Save button submits only instance fields, and every General setting (log_level, hard_max_per_cycle, max_history_rows, request_timeout, page_size, tracking_window_minutes, max_consecutive_failures, skip_unreleased) silently resets to its hardcoded default on every save. No OWASP-category vulnerability (injection/XSS/secrets/auth/SSRF/deserialization/mass-assignment) is introduced by this specific change since it's pure form-boundary restructuring with no new input handling, but this is a real functional/data-integrity regression that should be routed to a correctness/bugs reviewer rather than closed here.

No CSRF token is present on either <form> (save_settings or save_security) in either the before or after state of this diff; this is pre-existing and unchanged by this diff, so not reported as a new finding, but noted for completeness since the diff touches these exact forms.

The Security form (save_security, lines 97-114) sitting between General and the instances form is why a single literal <form> can't wrap both. The form= attribute is the correct way around that, and the diff offers no alternative such as adding a Save button to the General form.
No new imports, dependencies, or cross-module coupling. routes.py and the save_security handler are unaffected apart from the form-contract mismatch described in arch-001.
